data.title: Bally's lands key financing for its Bronx casino resort project
data.description:
Bally's Corporation (BALY) updated investors this week that its $560M financing package will help its planned $4B Bronx casino resort move forward. The funds will go toward pre-construction planning and help Bally's (BALY) stay on schedule while it completes the broader capital raise. The loan is expected to close during the current quarter, subject to approvals and customary conditions.

In its application materials in New York, Bally's (BALY) set a construction timeline of eight to nine months after securing a license and a single-phase opening sometime in 2030.

The project, known as Bally’s Bronx, is planned for a 16-acre portion of Bally’s Golf Links at Ferry Point near the Whitestone Bridge—land formerly associated with Trump Golf Links. Bally's (BALY) bought the key city-owned parcel for about $156.6M earlier this year, giving it control of the clubhouse, parking, and access areas needed for the development.

Plans call for a roughly 3M-square-foot, 19-story waterfront complex. Key elements include a casino with approximately 3,500 slot machines, about 210 table games and poker; a 500-room hotel; more than 10 food-and-beverage venues; a 2,000-person event or convention center; and about 4,600 parking spaces. Bally's (BALY) has also proposed retaining golf- and park-related amenities around the resort and investing more than $160M in nearby Ferry Point Park and Throggs Neck improvements.

data.title: Lilly to invest in QurCan as part of genetic medicines deal
data.description:
Canadian biotech QurCan Therapeutics on Tuesday announced an investment from Eli Lilly (LLY) as part of an exclusive research and collaboration agreement with the Indiana-based pharma giant to develop genetic medicines.

The deal focuses on leveraging QurCan’s TERP (Target-Engineered Responsive Polymer) platform to develop genetic medicines that target the central and peripheral nervous systems.

Under the agreement, QurCan will lead the initial research, after which Eli Lilly (LLY) will take over further research, clinical development, and commercialization.

The Toronto-based firm will receive an upfront payment and a strategic investment from Lilly (LLY) as part of the deal. Additionally, the company will be entitled to a per-program payment of up to $237M, which represents R&D support payments as well as research, development, and commercial milestone payments.

QurCan will also receive tiered royalties as a percentage of global net sales of commercialized products.

The multi-program collaboration marks Eli Lilly’s (LLY) latest as the weight-loss drugmaker looks to step up its deal-making activity driven by record-breaking sales from its obesity franchise. In late August, the company agreed to buy privately held Merida Biosciences for up to $2.9B in cash to boost its immunology portfolio.

data.title: Truist to exit near-prime auto lending business
data.description:
Truist Financial (TFC) on Tuesday disclosed it is exiting its near-prime auto lending business, having entered into an agreement to sell $5.5B of auto loans tied to Regional Acceptance Corporation.

The sale marks an exit from substantially all assets of Regional Acceptance.

The non-core, less profitable business sale generates for Truist $5.2B of net proceeds and a $535M loan loss reserve recapture. It creates $945M, or 22 basis points, of CET1 capital. The transaction reduces Truist's nonperforming loans by over 10 basis points as of June 30 and net charge-offs by ~10 basis points annually.

Proceeds are intended to be used to repay wholesale borrowings and reposition certain AFS (available-for-sale) securities.

The divestiture is expected to be modestly accretive to earnings and return on tangible common equity by 2027.

The transaction is expected to close in late third quarter or early fourth quarter.

Truist maintained its third quarter and full year 2026 financial guidance, excluding the impact of the strategic actions.

CFO Mike Maguire is scheduled to speak at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference at 10:30 AM ET today.

data.title: Lindblad acquires a controlling stake in a luxury Antarctic travel company
data.description:
Lindblad Expeditions Holdings (LIND) announced it has acquired a majority ownership of White Desert and Echo Charlie in the largest transaction in the company's history. A majority stake of 60% in White Desert and Echo Charlie was executed for an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $61M, plus approximately $6M for cash on the balance sheet and subject to customary true-up adjustments for working capital, cash, and indebtedness. 

Established in 2005 by record-breaking polar explorer Patrick Woodhead, White Desert flies clients into the remote interior of Antarctica, blending logistical precision with a level of comfort previously unheard of on the ice. Billed as the ultimate bucket-list adventure, their itineraries include a journey to the geographic South Pole and a visit to an emperor penguin colony of over 20K birds.

The company said the strategic acquisition marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter in Antarctic travel. Leveraging their shared expertise, Lindblad Expeditions and White Desert see significant opportunities to expand White Desert's extraordinary offering through the development of camps and guest experiences. 

Through its global platform and expertise, Lindblad Expeditions (LIND) said it will also support the development and growth of a brand-new offering called Echo Charlie. "Inspired by the golden age of aviation aboard a fully restored DC-3 (an aircraft that can land on remote airstrips without the hassle of commercial airports), this new offering fuses real-life adventure with the seamless connection of highly diverse landscapes," highlighted Lindblad (LIND).

Like other companies that have joined the Lindblad family, White Desert and Echo Charlie will continue to operate as a stand-alone offering, preserving their founder-led vision and distinctive culture while benefiting from the reach, capabilities, and resources of Lindblad Expeditions.

Lindblad Expeditions (LIND) also raises its full-year 2026 revenue, net yield, and adjusted EBITDA guidance to reflect the acquisitions of White Desert and Echo Charlie, as well as continued strong performance across the business. The current expectations for the full year 2026 are fortour revenue of $850M to $880M, net yield per available guest night of 5.5% to 6.5%, and adjusted EBITDA of $140M to $148M.

Shares of Lindblad (LIND) were up 0.5% in premarket trading.

data.title: Profusa clears Nasdaq compliance issues
data.description:
• Profusa (PFSA) said it has regained compliance with Nasdaq’s minimum bid price and equity requirements.
  • However, it will remain subject to a one-year mandatory Nasdaq monitoring period. If it fails to meet the equity requirement during that period, Nasdaq can issue a delisting determination without first allowing the company to submit a compliance plan.
  • The stock price traded about 9.8% lower on Tuesday pre-market hours.

data.title: KKR, Neuberger units to take minority stake in Datavant
data.description:
Neuberger Capital Solutions, Neuberger Private Markets, and KKR (KKR) have agreed to acquire a minority stake in Datavant, the health data collaboration platform, alongside existing investor New Mountain Capital, the companies said on Tuesday.

New Mountain Capital, a Datavant investor since 2014, will retain its control position. The transaction is expected to close in 4Q 2026. Financial terms of the minority stake acquisition were not disclosed.

"With New Mountain, Neuberger, and KKR by our side, we're well equipped to deepen our impact across the healthcare ecosystem and accelerate into our next phase of growth," said Kyle Armbrester, CEO of Datavant.

KKR is investing in Datavant primarily through funds and accounts managed by its Strategic Investments Group. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.

data.title: Rockwell Automation joins Anthropic’s Project Glasswing
data.description:
• Rockwell Automation (ROK) on Tuesday said it has joined Anthropic’s (ANTHRO) Project Glasswing, designed to advance AI-enabled cyber defense for industrial critical infrastructure.
  • Through controlled access to Claude Mythos 5, Rockwell security teams are exploring ways to accelerate the discovery, validation, prioritization, and remediation of vulnerabilities across software and connected systems that manufacturers rely on every day, the company said.
